„bei Ihrer Ankunft“ was misread as arrival at the destination. Now „sobald Sie dort ankommen“, which points back to the station. „On arrival“ is kept and the time is now unambiguous.

„kommen Sie“ had no destination. Added „zum Bahnhof“. This adds no fact: the operator fact is coming to the departure station, AR «احضر», EN "arrive". „vor der Abfahrt“ and „mindestens eine Stunde“ are unchanged.

„SAR-Personal“ / bare „SAR“ break termbase #375: in running text the operator is always „Bahngesellschaft SAR“, never bare „SAR“, because the same page uses „SAR“ for the currency (der Saudi-Riyal (SAR)). After the Uber sentence a bare „der Bahngesellschaft“ would also break with how the page names the operator at the start of a new paragraph (faq.1.a, train.paras.1). Disliking the repetition does not override a termbase ruling.

„brauchen“, „seien Sie … am Bahnhof“, „melden Sie sich gleich“: „gleich“ blurs "on arrival", and „sich melden“ turns "tell" into a check-in. The other changes are matters of taste, and 11a/11b already fix both problems the reader found. „benötigen“ keeps the register of the published page.
